reason: E1 and E2 support a strain-rate-dependent transition from thermally activated glide to phonon drag in other FCC HEAs, but neither study involves the Co-free FeNiCrMn alloy, so the key premise that this mechanism governs FeNiCrMn specifically is not directly supported by the cited evidence. The uniform FCC matrix premise is not addressed by the cited passages.
premises: A transition in dislocation mechanism from thermally activated glide to viscous phonon drag occurs at a strain rate around 10^3 s^-1 in FCC high-entropy alloys.
Phonon drag significantly increases yield strength and reduces ductility at high strain rates/low temperatures.
Thermally activated dislocation glide dominates at low strain rates/high temperatures, leading to lower flow stress and better ductility.
The FeNiCrMn alloy retains a uniform single-phase FCC matrix after solidification.
